subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is referenced by Zalthir as the authority who decides the fate of failed Drow.
source_quote: Grygum might decide his fate should be precisely like Serith's

subject: guard chamber
fact: The guard chamber contains a zurkhwood table, three chairs, a side table, and a Sava game set on the table.
source_quote: It contains a zurkhwood table and three chairs, a smaller side table, and a Sava game set on the table

subject: Ilvara
fact: Ilvara is referenced by Imbros as the authority who decides the fate of failed Drow.
source_quote: Ilvara might decide his fate should be precisely like Serith's

subject: the key
fact: The key had hung around Kalan Strongbranch's neck once.
source_quote: It had hung around Kalan Strongbranch's neck once

subject: the stolen sapphire
fact: The stolen sapphire carried a summoning working — it could pull an item to you, but only an item not in anyone's possession.
source_quote: The stolen sapphire carried a summoning working — it could pull an item to you, but only an item not in anyone's possession

subject: the poison book
fact: The poison book had a dead scholar and was the center of the murder investigation.
source_quote: There is a poisoned book and a dead scholar

subject: the Oak Tree Apothecary
fact: The Oak Tree Apothecary is between the Sea Warden's Tower and the House of Mechanus, a treehouse grown into the roots of an evergreen oak.
source_quote: The Oak Tree Apothecary, he said, between the Sea Warden's Tower and the House of Mechanus, a treehouse grown into the roots of an evergreen oak

subject: Leuwin
fact: Leuwin is a satyr druid, elderly and absent-minded, with a pet squirrel.
source_quote: A satyr druid named Leuwin, elderly and absent-minded, with a pet squirrel

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir said, 'Totally, totally,' in a voice that recorded everything.
source_quote: Totally, totally," Zalthir said, in a voice that recorded everything

subject: Daz
fact: Daz said, 'I can read it. A small divining touch — the least of the seeing-arts.'
source_quote: I can read it," I said. "A small divining touch — the least of the seeing-arts.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin said, 'Look, I'm just saying, if we solve the murder, we get any book in the place.'
source_quote: Look, I'm just saying, if we solve the murder, we get any book in the place.

subject: Daral
fact: Daral had the poison book and worked out someone wanted him to take the fall.
source_quote: He had the poison book. He'd worked out someone wanted him to take the fall.

subject: Fembris
fact: Fembris wanted to attend Grygum's debate in the Oval Theater.
source_quote: Fembris asked to leave. Our minder... wanted to attend a debate. Grygum's debate, as it turned out — a disputation in the Oval Theater

subject: Candlekeep
fact: Candlekeep is the world's most dangerous library.
source_quote: the world's most dangerous library

subject: the keep
fact: The keep has an active murder running through it.
source_quote: There is an active murder running through this keep.

subject: the dining room
fact: The dining room is where the meals were served, and where, if you were a poisoner, you'd have wanted to be.
source_quote: The dining room, for one. Where the meals were served, and where, if you were a poisoner, you'd have wanted to be.

subject: the research area
fact: The research area was suddenly full of rooms nobody would be watching.
source_quote: everyone was now headed toward the research area, which meant the keep was suddenly full of rooms nobody would be watching

subject: the Oval Theater
fact: The Oval Theater hosted Grygum's disputation on his new theology.
source_quote: a disputation in the Oval Theater on his new theology

subject: Janussi
fact: Janussi picked up the book at dinner, and at the time, it was wrapped.
source_quote: The book got picked up by Janussi at dinner. And at the time, it was wrapped.

subject: Kalan Strongbranch
fact: Kalan Strongbranch handed off the key rather than wear it, paranoid, maybe.
source_quote: Strongbranch handed his off rather than wear it. Paranoid, maybe.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool tried to help, an eye surfacing through the ooze, hopeful.
source_quote: Glabbagool tried to help, an eye surfacing through the ooze, hopeful

subject: Bookwyrm
fact: Bookwyrm herself was unable to politically afford to miss Grygum's debate.
source_quote: Bookwyrm herself unable to politically afford to miss it

subject: Kelemvor
fact: The followers of Kelemvor have made the point very clear, repeatedly, through their god's usual incomprehensible cryptic phrasing.
source_quote: The followers of Kelemvor have made that point very clear, repeatedly, through their god's usual incomprehensible cryptic phrasing.

subject: Bahamut
fact: Bahamut may or may not have been watching.
source_quote: Bahamut may or may not have been watching.

subject: the Underdark
fact: The Underdark teaches you that the people who kill you usually want it documented first.
source_quote: the Underdark teaches you that the people who kill you usually want it documented first

subject: Menzoberranzan
fact: A Menzoberranzan child should have closed the connection on reflex.
source_quote: a Menzoberranzan child should have closed on reflex

subject: the locket
fact: A locket from around the dead man's neck was taken, and we assume that inside that locket was the key.
source_quote: Some locket from around the dude's neck was taken. We assume that inside that locket was the key.

subject: the wrapping
fact: Daral was baffled we even asked about a magical seal. 'Why would I put a magical seal on the wrapping? It's a gift!'
source_quote: Why would I put a magical seal on the wrapping? It's a gift!

subject: the poison
fact: The poison turned black after the dead man's saliva mixed with it.
source_quote: When I mixed with his saliva, it turned black, okay?

subject: the summoning spell
fact: The summoning spell could retrieve an item through a keyed gem, provided you had the magic to call it.
source_quote: The summoning had been worked on a *different* key.

subject: the murder
fact: The murder involved a poisoned book, a stolen key, a stolen sapphire, and a dead scholar.
source_quote: There is a poisoned book and a dead scholar.

subject: the debate
fact: Grygum's debate on his new theology drew half the avowed and caused Fembris to abandon his post.
source_quote: Grygum's debate, as it turned out — a disputation in the Oval Theater on his new theology, with half the avowed already in attendance

subject: the gift-giving
fact: Daral dropped the book under the evergreen tree around 11am on Deadwinter's Eve, before rushing to the keeper's Tower.
source_quote: He'd dropped the book under the evergreen tree, next to the other gifts, around 11am on Deadwinter's Eve

subject: the search
fact: The search for the killer required looking for clear vials of poison, not black splashes.
source_quote: A vial of some sort of clear.

subject: the timeline reconstruction
fact: The timeline of the book's poisoning was critical: whether tampering occurred before or after Daral handed it over.
source_quote: the timeline of the book itself, whether it was poisoned before or after Daral handed it over.

subject: the key's magical test
fact: Daz tested the key with a divining touch and found it clean — not linked to the summoning spell.
source_quote: I took custody of the key, set my fingers to the cold iron of it, and let the spell read the object... The answer was no. The key was clean.

subject: the sapphire's purpose
fact: The sapphire was not decoration — it was the retrieval token for the summoning spell, requiring the same stone to store and recall.
source_quote: The sapphire isn't decoration: it's the retrieval token, and it has to be the *same* sapphire both to store and to recall.

subject: the gap in the account
fact: Daz could not resolve the connection between the gem, the key, and the murdered man — a pattern he could see but not name.
source_quote: I reached for it and came up with nothing. The pattern was there. I simply could not make it resolve... I will call it a gap in the account.

subject: the decision to prioritize the killer
fact: Thorin declared the priority was to find the killer, not who stole the key.
source_quote: And our priority is to find the killer, not who stole the key.

subject: the revelation of the poison's activation
fact: The poison only activated upon contact with a living thing's saliva — it was clear in vials and turned black after death.
source_quote: The stuff only wakes up when a living thing touches it.

subject: the abandonment of Fembris's post
fact: Fembris left his post to attend Grygum's debate, handing the party an hour without supervision.
source_quote: A keeper of the keep, leaving his post, to watch the orc argue dragons. I did not stop him.

subject: the handoff of the key to Daz
fact: The key was handed to Daz by the narrator, after having been held by Kalan Strongbranch.
source_quote: I handed it to Daz and let it become his problem.

subject: the revelation of the summoning's mechanism
fact: The summoning spell works by binding an item to a gem, and the item can only be retrieved if the gem is possessed and the caster has the magic to call it.
source_quote: Possess the gem and you possess the item, provided you have the magic to call it.

subject: the identification of Daral's motive
fact: Daral's motive was to prove he wasn't a murderer, and he offered to ward every gift if he survived the night.
source_quote: if he made it through the night, hint, hint, he'd see to it everyone wrapped their gifts right. Wards on every wrapping, the kind that bite the careless, for everyone.

subject: the discovery of the locket's contents
fact: The locket was assumed to contain the key, and its theft implied the killer intended to remove the key from the victim's possession.
source_quote: We assume that inside that locket was the key.

subject: the realization that the poison was not on the book
fact: The poison was not visible on the book because it activated only after ingestion, not on contact.
source_quote: Why did it turn dark, but it's not dark on the book? Because it goes black after you die.

subject: the naming of the gap
fact: Daz refused to call his inability to resolve the connection a failure — he called it a gap in the account.
source_quote: I will not call that a failure. I will call it a gap in the account.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is drow. Daz knew that world the way I know a tunnel's slope without thinking about it — and still the meaning slid off him. He'd forgotten everything that mattered and kept everything that didn't.
source_quote: Daz was drow. Daz knew that world the way I know a tunnel's slope without thinking about it — and still the meaning slid off him. He'd forgotten everything that mattered and kept everything that didn't.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool offered himself for the sneaking. *I have learned silence,* he said. *Am I being silent enough? Was this good silence, or was it too loud silence?*
source_quote: From the bag, Glabbagool offered himself for the sneaking. *I have learned silence,* he said. *Am I being silent enough? Was this good silence, or was it too loud silence?*

subject: Candlekeep
fact: The air in Candlekeep still smelled wrong to me. Not bad — paper, lamp oil, old stone warmed by sun I had not seen in months — just wrong, the way anything smells when you have spent too long breathing rock.
source_quote: The air in Candlekeep still smelled wrong to me. Not bad — paper, lamp oil, old stone warmed by sun I had not seen in months — just wrong, the way anything smells when you have spent too long breathing rock.

subject: Southern Dining Hall
fact: The dining hall still smelled like breakfast. Long tables, cleared but not reset, that particular morning-after smell of porridge and tallow gone cold.
source_quote: The dining hall still smelled like breakfast. Long tables, cleared but not reset, that particular morning-after smell of porridge and tallow gone cold.

subject: Milil's lead-lined chalice
fact: The brass cup in those open stone hands was lead-lined. Inside it: a heart. And a blood-stained meat cleaver.
source_quote: I went to the altar, took the chalice down out of those open hands, and looked inside. Photons don't care about lead. Whatever was in there, I'd see it. A heart. And a blood-stained meat cleaver.

subject: Janussi's heart
fact: Janussi's heart was found in the lead-lined chalice. Because they stole his heart. They didn't want anybody to be able to bring him back and ask him what happened.
source_quote: Janussi's heart," Daral said. "Because they stole his heart. They didn't want anybody to be able to bring him back and ask him what happened.

subject: blood-stained meat cleaver
fact: The blood-stained meat cleaver was found inside the lead-lined chalice alongside Janussi's heart.
source_quote: A heart. And a blood-stained meat cleaver.

subject: wrapping paper from Secret Santa
fact: The wrapping paper from the Secret Santa gift was dropped by Janussi in a wicker basket by the door on his way out — but turned up later in his office, not here.
source_quote: Janussi took his unwrapped, thanked his secret donor, and excused himself, dropping the wrapping paper in a wicker basket by the door on his way out. The wrapping paper turned up in Janussi's office, not here.

subject: Irony
fact: Irony said she always tells the truth — compulsively, without choice. 'I really hate it when people make that joke. I'm so sorry — this compulsive need to always tell the truth.'
source_quote: Are you being ironic?" I asked. Couldn't help it. "No!" she snapped. Then, flatter: "But I, you know, I really hate it when people make that joke. I'm so sorry — this compulsive need to always tell the truth.

subject: Sprig
fact: Sprig tasted all the food. 'Is she the poison taster?' I asked, and Irony said yes, like I should've known, and I hadn't.
source_quote: Then she told me to go talk to Sprig. Sprig tasted all the food. 'Is she the poison taster?' I asked, and Irony said yes, like I should've known, and I hadn't.

subject: Daral
fact: Daral threw his hands up. 'Maybe they wanted me to be blamed.'
source_quote: Daral threw his hands up. 'Maybe they wanted me to be blamed.'

subject: A'lai Aivenmore
fact: A'lai Aivenmore was the one who wanted the keep. The one about to be dismissed. The one who saw Daral's love of poetry, his love of fiction, as a threat to his approach to the universe.
source_quote: A'lai Aivenmore. The one who wanted the keep. The one about to be dismissed. The one who saw Daral's love of poetry, his love of fiction, as a threat to his approach to the universe.

subject: Midsummer Wine ritual
fact: Daral suddenly remembered: 'We used it for the Midsummer Wine!' — referring to the lead-lined chalice used to blind far-seeing magic.
source_quote: Daral didn't hear me. He'd gone still, staring at the statue, and then he came apart a little. 'Oh my goodness! We used it for the Midsummer Wine!'

subject: Deadwinter Supper
fact: The Deadwinter supper began at the 5PM bell. Twelve plates: beetroot soup, fried carp, smoked mackerel. Fruit compots, spiced wines and ales, honey, vodka, green tea. Served by three of them: Irony, Orrin, and Sprig.
source_quote: The Deadwinter supper began at the 5PM bell. Twelve plates: beetroot soup, fried carp, smoked mackerel. Fruit compots, spiced wines and ales, honey, vodka, green tea. Served by three of them: her, Orrin, and Sprig.

subject: Secret Santa gift exchange
fact: Sylvira Savikas stormed out, and Kazryn Nyantani took it on herself to hand out the gifts under the evergreen tree, gave each one to the matching great reader. Secret Santa, basically.
source_quote: Then Sylvira Savikas stormed out, and Kazryn Nyantani took it on herself to hand out the gifts under the evergreen tree, gave each one to the matching great reader. Secret Santa, basically.

subject: Janussi's office
fact: The wrapping paper from the Secret Santa gift turned up in Janussi's office, not in the wicker basket by the dining hall door.
source_quote: The wrapping paper turned up in Janussi's office, not here.

subject: Alkrist
fact: Alkrist was cheerful, pitching a project: *Tales of War by the Generals That Waged Them*, first-hand strategy from warlords and commanders around the world.
source_quote: Alkrist was cheerful, pitching a project: *Tales of War by the Generals That Waged Them*, first-hand strategy from warlords and commanders around the world.

subject: Teles
fact: Teles scoffed the project sounded as likely to succeed as some Fheminor Scrivenbark program.
source_quote: Teles scoffed the project sounded as likely to succeed as some Fheminor Scrivenbark program,

subject: Janussi
fact: Janussi praised Alkrist's project: 'the kind of knowledge that could benefit civilization,' and reminded the room that deciding which branches of knowledge to further was their privileged responsibility.
source_quote: Janussi praised it the other way: 'the kind of knowledge that could benefit civilization,' and reminded the room that deciding which branches of knowledge to further was their privileged responsibility.

subject: Poisoning of Janussi
fact: Janussi was poisoned by a book Daral had given him. And the whole thing was so ornate that it itched.
source_quote: Janussi was dead. Poisoned by a book Daral had given him. And the whole thing was so ornate that it itched.

subject: Attempt to grow a nose on Glabbagool
fact: I crouched by the bag one more time. The ooze had no nose. That seemed like a thing worth attempting. 'Can Glabbagool try to grow a nose and get a good smell of the poison?'
source_quote: I crouched by the bag one more time. The ooze had no nose. That seemed like a thing worth attempting. 'I doubt this is gonna work,' I said, 'but can Glabbagool try to grow a nose and get a good smell of the poison?'

subject: Janussi
fact: Janussi is the poison taster who died at midnight, her death collateral to the targeted poisoning, and the cut string on her Deadwinter gift was retied after being severed.
source_quote: The string tied around Janussi's Deadwinter gift had clearly been cut and retied.

subject: Sylvira Savikas
fact: Sylvira Savikas is a tiefling who was seen hunting by candlelight, pointed to her throat to indicate hoarseness, and was helped by Sprig to find a pot of honey before saying goodnight.
source_quote: She ran into Sylvira Savikas hunting for something by candlelight... the tiefling just pointed at her throat, too hoarse to talk. Sprig helped her find a pot of honey and said goodnight.

subject: Sprig
fact: Sprig is the poison taster who volunteered to sample all twelve dishes despite being told it wasn't necessary, and she assisted Sylvira Savikas by finding honey when she was hoarse.
source_quote: She'd volunteered to taste each one to make sure none was poisoned. The chefs told her it wasn't necessary. She insisted. Sprig helped her find a pot of honey and said goodnight.

subject: Alkrist
fact: Alkrist was observed holding a scrap of paper to a candle and feeding it to the flame, then dropping it when two junior avowed entered.
source_quote: Alkrist had been holding a small scrap of paper toward a candle, feeding it to the flame, and when two junior avowed walked in, he dropped it.

subject: Orrin Glass
fact: Orrin Glass is the deaf third waiter who noticed Alkrist burning a scrap of paper and reported the cut-and-retied string on Janussi's gift.
source_quote: Orrin handed me the one that mattered. Something out of the ordinary: the string tied around Janussi's Deadwinter gift had clearly been cut and retied.

subject: Teles Ahvoste
fact: Teles Ahvoste is one of the great readers who made advances toward Irony, prompting her to deflect attention toward Sprig.
source_quote: Teles Ahvoste. One of the other great readers, making passes at Irony.

subject: Irony
fact: Irony cannot lie but steered inquiry toward Sprig instead of answering directly, and was observed rolling her eyes at the junior avowed's attention.
source_quote: Irony can't lie. But she hadn't answered. She'd pointed us at Sprig instead. Can't lie isn't has to tell. She steered us rather than speak false.

subject: Candlekeep kitchens
fact: The Candlekeep kitchens were visited by Sprig late at night for cookies, where she encountered Sylvira Savikas searching by candlelight at one in the morning.
source_quote: Late that night, going to the kitchens for cookies, she'd run into Sylvira Savikas hunting for something by candlelight... One in the morning.

subject: Poison taster's station
fact: The poison taster's station was where Sprig sampled all twelve dishes prepared by the Candlekeep chefs, each one tested for poison despite being told it was unnecessary.
source_quote: Twelve dishes, the Candlekeep chefs, every word of it. She'd volunteered to taste each one to make sure none was poisoned.

subject: Non-Christmas Christmas tree
fact: The non-Christmas Christmas tree was the site where gifts — primarily books — were stacked, and where Alkrist burned a scrap of paper and the string on Janussi’s gift was cut and retied.
source_quote: I wanted to ask whether anybody'd seen a person messing with the pile under the — the non-Christmas Christmas Christmas tree... The cut string was the rock in the right place.

subject: Apothecary tree trunk
fact: The apothecary tree trunk housed Leuwin the satyr and Nibbles the squirrel, where a vial of dangerous toxins was broken and concealed with a peppermint-soaked rag.
source_quote: Under the top shelf I found a peppermint-soaked rag and a broken vial, and the shelf above the spillage was labeled, in Elvish, Dangerous Toxins.

subject: Greenhouse below apothecary
fact: The greenhouse below the apothecary was where Leuwin was occupied by A'lai, creating a diversion while the dragonborn stole the toxin upstairs.
source_quote: Leuwin took him down through the rear exit to the greenhouse below... While the dragonborn was upstairs, alone, breaking the vial.

subject: Cut and retied string
fact: The cut and retied string on Janussi's Deadwinter gift was the key physical evidence indicating internal tampering, not an outside attack.
source_quote: The string tied around Janussi's Deadwinter gift had clearly been cut and retied.

subject: Peppermint-soaked rag
fact: The peppermint-soaked rag was a poorly concealed attempt to mask the scent of the broken vial of dangerous toxins in the apothecary.
source_quote: Under the top shelf I found a peppermint-soaked rag and a broken vial...

subject: Dead rats in glass jars
fact: The dead rats in glass jars in Alkrist's chambers showed active study of poison effects, their skin blistered and risen into pustules.
source_quote: Sealed glass jars holding dead rats, their skin blistered and risen into pustules.

subject: 1001 Tashalian Nights
fact: The book 1001 Tashalian Nights, found on Alkrist’s bedside table with a bookmark on the tale of a poisoned magic horn, indicated his knowledge of lethal gifts.
source_quote: On the bedside table lay a book — black leather, stars and gold filigree... The bookmark sat on the tale of a military commander, poisoned by a gift of surrender — a magic horn whose mouthpiece had been coated in Midnight Tears.

subject: White doves in cage
fact: The white doves in A'lai’s cage, with five perches worn and only two birds present, indicated three recent message flights had been sent.
source_quote: The cage was built for five. Two birds sat in it. The feeding troughs, the droppings, the wear on five perches. There had been more than two.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool is a grey ooze who assisted Zalthir in searching the Readers' chambers, flowing where Zalthir could not reach and reacting with eager curiosity.
source_quote: Glabbagool. The ooze had come out of the bag eager... He flowed where I could not reach; I read what he could not understand.

subject: Candlekeep chefs
fact: The Candlekeep chefs prepared twelve dishes for the meal, and told Sprig her taster role was unnecessary, yet she insisted on sampling each one.
source_quote: Twelve dishes, the Candlekeep chefs, every word of it. She'd volunteered to taste each one to make sure none was poisoned. The chefs told her it wasn't necessary.

subject: Junior avowed
fact: The junior avowed were the witnesses to Alkrist burning a scrap of paper, and were the subject of Irony's redirected attention.
source_quote: Alkrist had been holding a small scrap of paper toward a candle... when two junior avowed walked in, he dropped it.

subject: Cutting and retieing of Janussi's gift string
fact: The cutting and retieing of Janussi's gift string occurred in the room under the non-Christmas Christmas tree, indicating an insider tampered with the package after it was wrapped.
source_quote: The cut string was the rock in the right place. Nobody came in from outside. This was somebody who'd been at the table.

subject: Dragonborn breaking the toxin vial
fact: The dragonborn broke the vial of dangerous toxins in the apothecary while Leuwin was distracted in the greenhouse, creating a diversion to steal the poison.
source_quote: While the dragonborn was upstairs, alone, breaking the vial.

subject: Alkrist burning the scrap of paper
fact: Alkrist burned a scrap of paper near a candle and dropped it when junior avowed entered, suggesting he was destroying evidence linking him to the plot.
source_quote: Alkrist had been holding a small scrap of paper toward a candle, feeding it to the flame, and when two junior avowed walked in, he dropped it.

subject: Sprig assisting Sylvira with honey
fact: Sprig helped Sylvira Savikas find a pot of honey after Sylvira pointed to her throat, indicating hoarseness, and then said goodnight at one in the morning.
source_quote: Sprig helped her find a pot of honey and said goodnight. One in the morning.

subject: The poison taster
fact: The poison taster — Sprig — was the thread pulled first because her presence at the meal made her a potential target or witness to the poisoning.
source_quote: The food was the thread I pulled first. Irony pointed me at it.

subject: The book
fact: The book was the thread referenced by Irony and Orrin, as the poisoned gift and the burned paper both tied back to a book or written evidence.
source_quote: It was the book. Alkrist's point led to the book... The book sitting wrapped in that package...

subject: The non-Christmas Christmas tree
fact: The non-Christmas Christmas tree was the thread connecting the wrapped gifts, the cut string, and the burned paper, all occurring in its shadow.
source_quote: The cut string was the rock in the right place. Nobody came in from outside. This was somebody who'd been at the table.

subject: The apothecary vial
fact: The apothecary vial of dangerous toxins was the thread linking the dragonborn’s actions, the peppermint rag, and the poisoning method.
source_quote: Under the top shelf I found a peppermint-soaked rag and a broken vial, and the shelf above the spillage was labeled, in Elvish, Dangerous Toxins.

subject: The squirrel's testimony
fact: The squirrel's testimony was the thread that revealed the diversion by the drow and the theft by the dragonborn, separating the actors from the poison.
source_quote: The drow draws the druid downstairs... The dragonborn does the upstairs work and the handling of a substance that might kill you.

subject: The message doves
fact: The message doves in A'lai's cage were the thread indicating three recent communications, suggesting coordination beyond the immediate scene.
source_quote: The cage was built for five. Two birds sat in it. There had been more than two. Three messages had gone somewhere, and recently.

subject: The bookmark in 1001 Tashalian Nights
fact: The bookmark in 1001 Tashalian Nights was the thread revealing Alkrist’s specific interest in poison delivered via gifts — the magic horn of Midnight Tears.
source_quote: The bookmark sat on the tale of a military commander, poisoned by a gift of surrender — a magic horn whose mouthpiece had been coated in Midnight Tears.

subject: locked safe
fact: The locked safe is noted by Daz without regret: we are not the famed Whistler, no safecracker of that old generation among us. The safe stays shut.
source_quote: Daz would note it without regret: we are not the famed Whistler, no safecracker of that old generation among us. The safe stays shut.

subject: safe
fact: The opening was a finger's width, no more — a true safe, not one of the old massive locks a body could pour itself through.
source_quote: The opening was a finger's width, no more — a true safe, not one of the old massive locks a body could pour itself through.

subject: tower
fact: The tower was fighting me. Her chambers took half the top floor — comfortable, neatly arranged, no extravagance to it.
source_quote: Bookwyrm last, and by then the tower was fighting me. Her chambers took half the top floor — comfortable, neatly arranged, no extravagance to it.

subject: room
fact: The room was clean. That, too, was information.
source_quote: Glabbagool tasted the air and found no poison in it. A clean room. That, too, was information.

subject: cage
fact: A cage missing three birds.
source_quote: A cage missing three birds.

subject: jars
fact: Jars of blistered rats.
source_quote: Jars of blistered rats.

subject: page
fact: A page marked to a poisoning by gift.
source_quote: A page marked to a poisoning by gift.

subject: Midnight Tears
fact: I kept the name where I would not lose it.
source_quote: Midnight Tears. I kept the name where I would not lose it.
